---
title: "How it works"
---

## The superpopulation

Covariates come from a **Gaussian copula structured as a DAG**: every variable has
a latent standard normal; those without parents are jointly normal with the
scenario's correlations, the others are linear in their parents' latents
(standardised path coefficients) plus noise. Each latent is mapped to its marginal
by the quantile function (NORTA): exact marginals (truncated to their range if
given) with the intended dependence. **Rules** then tie variables together:
probabilities that depend on other variables, structural values and formulas.

People are generated in chunks of 5000 with seeds derived from the seed, the
scenario and the chunk, so person *k* is the same whatever the design or the sample
size, and a student key changes the seed.

## Outcomes and calibration

- binary: logistic model; events: Weibull proportional hazards (inverse transform);
  continuous: linear (optionally on the log scale); counts: Poisson or negative
  binomial.
- The intercept, or the baseline hazard, is **calibrated** on 100 000 simulated
  people so the population has the scenario's prevalence, rate, risk at a time,
  median or mean.
- Each person has their own outcome noise, shared by their treated and untreated
  versions, so trials compare potential outcomes of the same people.

## Designs

| design | sampling |
|---|---|
| cross-sectional | the first *n* people |
| cohort, prognosis | follow-up with administrative censoring, loss to follow-up, staggered entry |
| case-control | cases (events within a risk window) from as much population as needed, controls from the non-cases |
| matched case-control | controls matched exactly on categorical variables and within a caliper on numeric ones |
| randomised trial | permuted blocks, treatment effect on the outcome, follow-up for events |
| 2×2 crossover | sequences AB/BA, within-subject correlation, period and carryover effects |

## The answer key

The *true model* lists the effects used. The *expected estimates* come from one
large study of the same design (20 000 rows; 1500–3000 cases for case-control
designs), analysed with the model a student would fit: logistic, conditional
logistic, Cox, linear (with subject effects in a crossover) or Poisson; crude for
each variable and adjusted for all measured ones.

## Source

The engine is plain R (`R/engine_*.R`), independent of jamovi and tested with
`testthat`; the options panel is tested by driving jamovi in Docker with
Playwright. Code: [github.com/victor-moreno/jamovi-studysim](https://github.com/victor-moreno/jamovi-studysim).
